scripts.description:
Migration from System.Communication 3.0.3 to 3.1.0.

This migration unifies the adapter and pipeline type hierarchies:
- EdgeAdapter and MeshAdapter are merged into Adapter
- EdgePipeline and MeshPipeline are merged into Pipeline
- DataPipelineTrigger is renamed to PipelineTrigger

All existing EdgeAdapter/MeshAdapter entities become Adapter entities.
All existing EdgePipeline/MeshPipeline entities become Pipeline entities.
All existing DataPipelineTrigger entities become PipelineTrigger entities.

scripts.description:
Migration from System.Communication 3.35.0 to 4.0.0 (AB#4924).

Renames the CK type Pool to DeploymentSite. The type never described a pool of
anything: it is the LOCATION a workload is deployed to ("Default Cloud",
"k8sfirmianstrasse"), and the operator serving that location registers against it.
The name became actively dangerous in 4.0.0, which introduces AdapterPool — a real
pool of adapter processes. Two unrelated concepts called "Pool" in one model is the
kind of ambiguity that gets read wrong during an incident, so the rename ships WITH
the feature that would otherwise collide with it: one major bump and one migration
for the estate instead of two (concept §8, Q16 + Q18).

The association role linking a workload to its site is renamed in the SAME migration:
Manages / ManagedBy -> Hosts / HostedBy. A deployment location does not "manage"
anything — the Communication Operator does — so the old role name described the
relationship backwards, and fixing the type name while leaving the role would have
guaranteed a second major migration later (concept §8, Q18: the estate migrates once).

Every existing Pool entity becomes a DeploymentSite entity: rtId, rtWellKnownName and
attribute values are preserved, only the CkTypeId changes.

🔴 Both halves of every existing edge have to be rewritten, and for different reasons:

  - ChangeCkType rewrites the stored originCkTypeId / targetCkTypeId on associations.
    The engine does this automatically as part of the step (see
    TenantRepository.UpdateAssociationCkTypeIdsForMigrationAsync) — verified, not assumed.

  - RenameAssociationRole rewrites the stored associationRoleId. NOTHING does this
    automatically: the role id is persisted on every edge and no other transform touches
    it. Without this step every deployment-site-to-workload edge in every tenant would be
    orphaned SILENTLY — the model would no longer define the role the data refers to, the
    navigation would simply return nothing, and no error would be raised anywhere. The
    transform did not exist in the CK engine and was added for this migration.

🔴 The seeded entity's rtWellKnownName is renamed too, in step 3. That name is IDENTITY,
not display text: the service-managed blueprints re-apply against it. Renaming it in the
seed ALONE would create a SECOND deployment site on every tenant and silently orphan the
adapters attached to the first — so the seed change and the data change ship together, in
this migration. The step needed a new CK engine transform, SetWellKnownName, because the
well-known name is a field on the entity rather than a CK attribute.

steps.description: Change CkTypeId from Pool to DeploymentSite for all Pool entities
Rename association role Manages to Hosts on every stored edge
Rename the seeded deployment site's well-known name from CommunicationPool

types.description: An external client that connects via SignalR to execute data pipelines. Adapters are assigned to a deployment site and receive pipeline configurations from the Communication Controller. Deployed to Kubernetes by the Communication Operator via Helm (chart/values inherited from DeployableWorkload). An adapter with LifecycleMode = Leased has no process of its own and borrows one per work item from an AdapterPool in another tenant (AB#4924).

A pool of interchangeable adapter processes owned by one tenant and leased to tenants in its subtree, one work item per lease (AB#4924). The pool declares how many members may exist (MinReplicas..MaxReplicas), how big each member is, what queue pressure starts another one, and which tenants may borrow. Members are replicas of this one workload rather than separate entities: a lease binds a member to a tenant for the duration of one work item and the member retains nothing tenant-scoped afterwards. Not to be confused with DeploymentSite, which is where a workload is deployed and which was itself called Pool before 4.0.0.
Configuration for AI services (e.g. Anthropic Claude API). Stores API credentials and default model settings. Referenced by pipeline nodes via ApiKeyConfigurationName.

A tenant-specific web application deployed by the Communication Operator via Helm. Examples: energy-community, voest-app, maco-app. Most configuration (URIs, env vars, secrets) lives in ValuesYaml / Values inherited from DeployableWorkload; only operator-relevant fields are exposed as typed attributes. Ingress (IngressEnabled + Hostname) is inherited from DeployableWorkload.
A logical grouping of pipelines and triggers that belong together. DataFlows organize the data integration logic within a tenant.
Maps a source entity attribute to a target entity attribute with optional expression transformation
Abstract base type for entities that can be deployed to adapters or pools. Tracks deployment state, name, description, and status messages.

Abstract base type for workloads that the Communication Operator deploys to Kubernetes via Helm. Carries the chart reference, base values.yaml, and structured value overrides shared by Adapter and Application.

A deployment location that the Communication Operator serves — a cloud environment or a named edge site. Workloads are assigned to a site via the Hosts role, and the operator responsible for the site registers via SignalR to deploy and monitor them. Renamed from `Pool` in 4.0.0; the old name described a grouping the type never had and collided with the adapter pool introduced by AB#4924.
Configuration for Discord bot integration used by the ToDiscord pipeline node (POST /channels/{id}/messages).
IMAP email receiver configuration for polling a mailbox
SMTP email sender configuration for outgoing email delivery.
Configuration for EDA integration
Configuration for an energy community
Configuration for the finAPI banking adapter connection.
Configuration for Grafana integration. Used by the GrafanaProvisionTenant and GrafanaDeprovisionTenant pipeline nodes.

Configuration of a Helm chart repository (HTTP, typically GitHub Pages — public or private). Referenced by DeployableWorkload entities so the Communication Operator knows where to pull the chart from. Tenant-scoped.

A borrower-local mirror of an AdapterPool owned by an ancestor or sibling tenant (AB#5271). Exists so a borrowing tenant can see, list and reference the pools lent to it, none of which is possible against an entity in another tenant database. Display and association only: the lease-time decision always re-reads the lending tenant's own pool, so this mirror can never widen what a borrower is allowed to use. Provisioned and kept in sync by the Communication Controller; never author-set.
Configuration for connecting to a Loxone Miniserver via REST API
Microsoft Graph API configuration for OAuth2 client credentials authentication
A data processing pipeline that defines a sequence of processing nodes. Pipelines are deployed to adapters for execution and can be organized within data flows.

Records an individual pipeline execution with its status, timing, trigger type, and optional input/output data. Linked to the executed pipeline and the adapter that performed the execution. On a leased adapter pool (AB#4924) the entity exists from the moment the work item is enqueued, so one work item is one PipelineExecution from Queued through Running to completion.

Aggregated execution statistics for a pipeline across multiple time windows (rolling 60 min; 12, 24 and 720 UTC clock hours including the current partial hour — the latter three are exactly the sum of HourlyBuckets over the window, AB#5583). Tracks success/failure counts and average duration per period.
A scheduled trigger that executes one or more pipelines based on a cron expression. Organized within data flows alongside the pipelines they trigger.
The SAP configuration type is used to configure the connection to an SAP system.
Client credentials for service-to-service authentication (OAuth2 client credentials grant)
Configuration for connecting to an SFTP server. Supports password and private key authentication.

Tenant-owned Signal phone-number channel (AB#5143). Exactly ONE per tenant (singleton, enforced by the Communication Controller service layer), and a number may be claimed by only one tenant per instance. Managed exclusively through the tenant self-service REST endpoints ({tenant}/v1/signal/channel) — the controller is the only component allowed to talk to the unauthenticated signal-cli-rest-api bridge.
A label that can be associated with any entity for categorization and filtering purposes.
Configuration for the WeClapp cloud ERP API connection. Stores the tenant-specific base URL and API key. Referenced by WeClapp adapter nodes via apiConfiguration.

associationRoles.description: Links a pipeline execution record to the pipeline that was executed.
Links a pipeline to the adapter that executes it. Each pipeline is executed by exactly one adapter.
Links a pipeline execution record to the adapter that performed the execution.

Links a deployable workload (Adapter / Application) to the Helm chart repository it pulls its chart from. Separate from the generic Uses role so the inverse view on HelmRepositoryConfiguration does not collide with Pipeline.Uses — keeping HelmRepositoryConfiguration as a regular SystemConfigurationInterface implementer in the generated GraphQL schema.
Links a deployment site to the workloads deployed there. A workload is hosted by at most one site. Renamed from Manages/ManagedBy in 4.0.0 together with the target type Pool -> DeploymentSite.

Links a borrowing adapter to the local mirror of the adapter pool it leases members from. An adapter borrows from at most one pool; one mirror serves every adapter in the tenant that borrows from that pool. Replaces the LentFromTenantId/LentFromAdapterPoolRtId attributes of 4.0.0.
Links a DataPointMapping to its source data point entity
Links a DataPointMapping to its target domain entity
Links a data source entity to a target domain entity for value propagation

Links an Adapter to the ServiceAccountConfiguration whose client credentials its pipelines execute under (AB#5027). Acts as the adapter-wide default; a single pipeline may override it by linking its own ServiceAccountConfiguration through the generic Uses role. Separate from Uses so the inverse view on Configuration stays Pipeline-scoped and SystemConfigurationInterface survives in the generated GraphQL schema.

Links an adapter pool to the service account its members authenticate with when they open the management connection to the pool hub. Not the identity work runs under — that comes from the borrower's own account, carried on each lease.
Links a pipeline to downstream pipelines that receive its output data for chained processing.
Links a pipeline statistics record to the pipeline it aggregates metrics for. Each pipeline has at most one statistics record.
Links a tag to the entities it labels for categorization and filtering.
Links a pipeline trigger to the pipelines it starts on schedule.
Links a pipeline to the configurations it requires for execution (e.g. connection settings for external systems).

attributes.description: JSON-serialized adapter-specific configuration that is deployed to the adapter. Entered by the tenant and may hold credentials, so it is owned by the tenant - a blueprint update or re-apply keeps the stored value and only initialises a new adapter - and it is not carried in an ExportRt.

Whether and to whom an adapter pool lends its members, i.e. which part of the tenant tree may be handed a lease on it (AB#4924). NotShared (default) makes the pool private to its owning tenant, which is a legitimate configuration — a pool is still useful as a way to run one tenant's own workloads elastically. The trust direction is fixed by the tenant tree and is never configurable upwards: a descendant can not lend to its ancestors (concept §3).
Grafana Server Admin password.
Grafana Server Admin username for organization management API.

AI model identifier to use (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-1). Mandatory and has no default: a pinned model id goes out of date (a retired "-20250514" snapshot returns HTTP 404), so it must be set explicitly on each AiConfiguration.

Whether the identity client carries the on-behalf-of delegation grant (urn:meshmakers:params:oauth:grant-type:on-behalf-of, AB#5026/AB#5031). Absent means true — the pre-AB#5111 behaviour, where every provisioned pipeline service account got the grant. Set to false to make the account strictly client_credentials.
API key for authenticating with an external service (e.g. Anthropic sk-ant-... key, WeClapp API token). Stored as configuration attribute, not exposed in pipeline data context.

Base URL of the cluster-shared signal-cli-rest-api bridge this channel is registered against (e.g. http://signal-cli-rest-api.signal-bridge.svc.cluster.local:8080). The bridge API is unauthenticated; only the Communication Controller may call it.

What this repository serves — Adapters (adapter and platform charts) or Applications (tenant-app charts). AB#5295: unlike Channel this DOES drive behaviour: a DeployableWorkload with no HelmRepository association is resolved to the tenant's single repository whose purpose matches the workload type (Adapter/AdapterPool -> Adapters, Application -> Applications). Optional and without a default on purpose — a repository that does not declare its purpose is never chosen by that fallback, so tenants seeded before this attribute keep their exact previous behaviour until the channel blueprint stamps it.

Hours before FoldedBefore are folded history; hours at or after it are recomputed from the retained executions on every statistics sweep. The 12h/24h/30d counters are exactly the sum of these buckets over the window (AB#5583).

Last configuration error message. Set when ConfigurationState transitions to Error, cleared automatically when ConfigurationState transitions to Configured. Other state transitions (Pending, Unconfigured) leave this field untouched. Tracked separately from LastDeploymentError because configuration and deployment errors have independent root causes and must not mask each other.

UTC time of the last status report that was a success (e.g. a mail poll that completed). Unlike StatusMessage it is NOT overwritten by an error report, so "last succeeded at" survives a failing streak. Empty until the first successful status report. Written by the controller's status reporting (AB#5618), which today covers pipelines only; a report counts as a success unless it is flagged as an error or its line starts with "ERROR ".
Last synced sequence number for offline sync
Timestamp of the last value update for this data point
When statistics were last calculated

Timestamp when a pool member was assigned this execution's tenant (AB#4924) — "when did it actually start" as opposed to "when did it stop waiting to be scheduled". Concept §8 Q5. Written on the Queued -> Running transition together with LeaseWaitMs. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

Timestamp when the pool member was handed back after this execution (AB#4924) — "how long did it hold the process". LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt is the span a member was held for one tenant, and concept §4b makes that span, multiplied by the pool's per-member sizing, the exact consumption attributed to the borrowing tenant. It is therefore a BILLING input, not only a diagnostic: it must be stamped on the release path including the TTL-expiry and crash paths, where FinishedAt may never arrive. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

Milliseconds the work item spent waiting for a lease (AB#4924), i.e. LeaseGrantedAt - QueuedAt, written once when the lease is granted. Stored rather than derived so it survives the AB#4370 execution fold, which erases the raw execution and keeps only the statistics — without it the queue latency of a leased pool would be unmeasurable a few hours after the fact. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

RtId of the AdapterPool inside LeasedFromTenantId that served this execution (AB#4924). Bare 24-character hexadecimal RtId. Recorded per execution rather than read back from the adapter's LentFromPoolRtId because the borrowing adapter can be re-pointed at a different pool later, and a cost report over past executions must reflect where the work actually ran.

The lending tenant whose adapter pool served this execution (AB#4924). Written when the lease is granted. Together with LeasedFromPoolRtId it is what makes concept §4b's attribution exact: consumption is billed to the tenant whose work ran — this execution's own tenant — and the pool named here is where the per-member sizing that prices it comes from. Unset on a dedicated (AlwaysOn / OnDemand) adapter, which never leases.

Identity of the individual pool member (the process) that held the lease for this execution (AB#4924). This is what concept §5 calls "an association from the execution to the assigned member" — it can NOT be an association, because the member belongs to the lending tenant's database and this execution to the borrower's (see the file header). It is also not an RtId: members are replicas of one pool workload, not separate entities, so the value is the member's stable runtime identity (its pool-hub registration id). It exists so the per-adapter queue view — "what is this member holding, what waits behind it" — can be projected out of the pool queue.
The lending tenant and pool this mirror stands for (AB#5271). Single-valued: a mirror has exactly one lender. Set and cleared as one unit, so a tenant id can never be present without its pool RtId.

Member of the LenderReference record (AB#5271): the bare 24-character hexadecimal RtId of the AdapterPool inside LenderTenantId. Names the POOL, never an individual member — membership is elastic, so a reference to a member would dangle the moment that member is drained.

Member of the LenderReference record (AB#5271): the tenant that owns the lent AdapterPool. Mirrored from the lending side; never author-set. The controller re-resolves it on every lease, so a stale value produces a refused deploy with a named reason rather than a wrong grant.

Optional allow-list narrowing the tenants an adapter pool with AdapterSharingMode != NotShared lends to (AB#4924). Absent or empty means "every tenant the sharing mode resolves to". A listed tenant that the sharing mode does NOT resolve to is ignored, never granted — the allow-list is an INTERSECTION with the tenant subtree, never a way around it, so the lending scope can not be widened past the trust boundary the tenant tree establishes.

Optional upper bound on how many of this pool's leases a single borrowing tenant may hold at the same time (AB#4924). Unset means no per-tenant cap — MaxReplicas and the round-robin rotation are the real bounds, which is why concept §8 Q11 deliberately left it without a default rather than inventing a number. Set it where one borrower is known to produce bursts (concept §6, "A borrowed tenant floods the queue"). It caps CONCURRENCY, not queue depth: excess work items stay Queued and visible in all three surfaces instead of being rejected.

Deployment state of the lending pool as last mirrored (AB#5271). A pool that is not Deployed cannot serve a lease, so this is the one mirrored field that explains a queue that never drains. Mirrored rather than resolved on read because the borrower cannot query the lender's database.
Upper bound of the lending pool's replica range as last mirrored (AB#5271). Informational, as above.

Lower bound of the lending pool's replica range as last mirrored (AB#5271). Informational: it tells a borrower how much capacity is kept warm, which is what decides whether a lease is likely to be immediate or queued.

The lending pool's sharing mode as last mirrored (AB#5271). Shown so a borrower can see WHY a pool is available to it. 🔴 Display only: the lease-time decision always re-reads the lender's own pool and calls MayLendAsync, so a borrower editing this value in its own database changes what it sees, never what it may use.

Lifecycle policy of the workload (AB#4914). AlwaysOn (default) keeps it running permanently; OnDemand allows the controller to scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand; Leased borrows a process from an adapter pool per work item (AB#4924). Runtime-state (AB#5301): an operator decision about the deployed workload, preserved across blueprint re-apply — a blueprint may seed it, but a re-apply never resets it.

Runtime lifecycle state of the workload (AB#4914): Running, Draining, Hibernated, or Waking. Written exclusively by the Communication Controller (idle watchdog and wake gates). Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply — resetting a Hibernated workload to Running would break the offline-is-expected semantics.
Optional mXparser expression to transform the source value. Variable value contains the source value.
Resolved mapping targets for data acquisition. Populated automatically by the BuildMappingTargets pipeline node from DataPointMappings.
The maximum number of concurrent connections is the maximum number of connections that can be established with an external system at the same time.

Hard ceiling on adapter pool members (AB#4924). The pool never starts a member beyond this count no matter what the queue does — a pool that could grow without bound would reintroduce, as a cluster-capacity incident, exactly the per-tenant process sprawl this feature exists to remove. When the ceiling is reached the queue simply grows and stays visible in all three surfaces (concept §6, "Pool exhausted"): scale the pool, or move the tenant to a dedicated adapter.
Maximum number of tokens for the AI response.
URL of the OctoMesh MCP server for AI tool use (e.g. https://localhost:5017). The tenant ID is appended automatically.

Lower bound on adapter pool members (AB#4924). The default of 1 is the point of the pool: one member stays hot, so the FIRST work item of the day does not pay a cold start — which is exactly the cost that makes plain OnDemand unattractive for periodic work (adapter boot 13 s, or 4.2 s with the AB#4920 warm-up). 0 is permitted and turns the pool into a scale-to-zero pool where every burst pays one cold start; choose it only where work is genuinely rare.
Optional display name for the tag.
ID of the network partner (Marktpartner
The neutral color of the theme
Email address for notifications related to EDA processes and messages
OAuth client ID for the Grafana datasource plugin.
URL of the OctoMesh Asset Repository for provisioned datasource configuration.

Human-readable reasons why the workload is not OnDemandCapable (AB#4984), e.g. "pipeline X uses process-bound trigger FromPolling@1". Empty when OnDemandCapable=true. Computed by the Communication Controller; shown in the Studio next to the LifecycleMode setting. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

Whether the workload can safely run with LifecycleMode=OnDemand (AB#4984): true iff none of its deployed pipelines uses a process-bound trigger (e.g. FromPolling, FromWatchRtEntity) that would silently stop at 0 replicas. Computed by the Communication Controller from the registered node descriptors on adapter registration and pipeline deploy. Runtime-state: written exclusively by the controller, preserved across blueprint re-apply.
Optional output data (JSON) from pipeline execution result
The password is the secret that is used to authenticate with the external system.
Dotted Helm values path for a ValueOverride entry (e.g. image.tag, service.port, oauth.clientId).
Phone number in E.164 format (+ followed by digits, e.g. +436641234567). Unique per OctoMesh instance: exactly one tenant may claim a number.
JSON-serialized pipeline node graph that defines the data processing logic.

Scheduling class of this pipeline on a leased adapter pool (AB#4924), derived from its trigger node on save. Interactive is work a human is waiting for, Batch is everything scheduled or event-driven; within one tenant's turn in the round-robin rotation Interactive is served first, and across tenants the class has no effect at all. Default Batch: a pipeline whose trigger declares no class must never jump a queue. Computed and persisted rather than author-set, exactly like OnDemandCapable — the trigger-node descriptor contract carries the class the way it already carries RequiresRunningProcess (AB#4914 §5), so the reflection-based descriptor scan picks it up and future or third-party nodes self-describe without a controller-side list. Meaningful only for pipelines deployed to a Leased adapter; harmless and ignored everywhere else.
Interval in seconds between polling cycles.
Kubernetes CPU limit of each pool member, e.g. "1" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberCpuRequest for why this is one value per pool and why it is a string.

Kubernetes CPU request of EACH pool member, e.g. "200m" (AB#4924). One sizing per pool, applied identically to every member it starts (concept §8, Q15) — members are interchangeable by construction, so per-member sizing would have no meaning: the scheduler can hand any lease to any member. Absent means the chart default applies. A string rather than a number because Kubernetes quantities are a notation ("200m", "1", "1.5"), and re-deriving that notation from a number is how sizing bugs get introduced.

Kubernetes memory limit of each pool member, e.g. "1Gi" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberMemoryRequest. Size it against the LARGEST tenant that may borrow the pool, not the average: a member serves one tenant at a time but serves each of them in full. AB#5330, measured: a member idles around 124 MiB and gains ~2 MiB per leased run, but the FIRST ExecuteCSharp@1 run costs it ~330 MiB permanently (the Roslyn compiler platform, loaded once per process and never released). A pool whose borrowers may run C# therefore needs at least 1Gi; at 512Mi the member is OOM-killed on the next lease it accepts, and because members are shared it takes another tenant's work down with it.

Kubernetes memory request of each pool member, e.g. "512Mi" (AB#4924). This is the number the whole feature is measured against: the prod-1 baseline in concept §1 is 170-200 Mi of pure .NET runtime per process for tenants that execute NOTHING, and a pool exists to stop paying that per tenant. Together with the lease spans (LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt) it is also what prices a borrower's consumption in concept §4b, so it is read for attribution and not only for scheduling.

Which queue signal starts another member (AB#4924). Default QueueDepthOrWaitSeconds. Scaling is driven by the queue and never by CPU: a member waiting for a lease is I/O-bound, so its CPU utilisation carries no information about whether work is piling up behind it (concept §4a).
The port number is the number of the port on which the external system is listening for incoming connections.
The primary color of the theme
The private key is a secret key that is used in asymmetric encryption to authenticate with the external system.
The private key passphrase is a secret that is used to protect the private key.
Price per kWh for producers in the energy community

Timestamp when the work item entered the pool queue (AB#4924). Set together with ExecutionStatus=Queued on a Leased workload and never overwritten afterwards, so QueuedAt..LeaseGrantedAt is the queue wait. Unset on a dedicated adapter, which is created Running.

When true, the Communication Operator injects cluster-internal credentials (MongoDB user/admin passwords, CrateDB password) into the workload's Helm release as secret-flagged value overrides. Applies to Adapters and Applications (e.g. backend services that talk to the core MongoDB / CrateDB). Defaults to false so untrusted or edge workloads do not receive cluster credentials by accident; enable only for workloads that run in the same cluster as the OctoMesh core services and need to talk to them directly. The RabbitMQ broker password is NOT controlled by this flag — it is injected unconditionally because every workload needs the controller-to-workload command bus.
UTC timestamp of the successful verification (transition to Registered).
What was attempted and how it ended (SignalRegistrationAction: RegisterRequested, RegisterFailed, CodeVerified, VerifyFailed, Deleted, DeleteFailed).
UTC timestamp of the audited registration attempt (SignalRegistrationEvent record).
Outcome detail of the audited attempt, e.g. the bridge message ("captcha required", "rate limited (retry after 30s)", "wrong code") or "registered" on a successful verification.
Acting user of the audited attempt, resolved from the authenticated principal: display name and/or subject id ("Name (subject)"), or "unknown" for a principal without either claim.

Capped audit trail of registration attempts (AB#5143): SignalRegistrationEvent records, newest first, the newest 50 kept. Appended server-side only; deleted together with the definition (a fresh definition starts with a fresh history).
Current registration state of the number against the Signal bridge. Driven by the register/verify/delete self-service flow (AB#5143).
HTTP(S) URL of a Helm repository index, e.g. https://meshmakers.github.io/octo-helm-core (public) or a private GitHub Pages site.
A client is a tenant instance in an SAP system. SAP is multi-tenant, which means that multiple organizations or departments can work on the same system without sharing data with each other.
An SAP gateway host is a server that provides communication services between SAP systems or between SAP systems and external applications.
An SAP gateway service provides communication services that are used between SAP systems or between SAP systems and external applications.
The language key is a two-character code that identifies the language in which the user interface is displayed.
A program ID is a unique identifier that is used to register a program on an SAP gateway server.
The registration count is the number of times a program is registered on an SAP gateway server.
The trace level is a number that determines the amount of information that is logged during communication with the SAP system.

Number of work items waiting for a lease that makes the pool start another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the depth signal (AB#4924). Measured across the whole pool queue, not per borrowing tenant — the pool scales because IT is saturated, whereas a single tenant's burst is bounded by round-robin and LendingMaxConcurrentLeasesPerTenant instead.

How long the OLDEST waiting work item may wait before the pool starts another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the wait signal (AB#4924). Catches the case depth alone misses: two items behind one long-running lease never reach a depth threshold but can still wait for minutes. Concept §8 Q14 leaves the averaging window over which this is evaluated to be MEASURED during implementation rather than guessed, which is why the threshold is configuration and not a constant.
The secondary color of the theme
Email address used as the sender (From) for outgoing emails.

Profile display name of the account, shown to Signal users instead of "Unknown". Pushed to the bridge (PUT /v1/profiles/{number}) when the channel reaches Registered (verify success or adoption) and on the displayName self-service endpoint (which also clears it — without a bridge call, since Signal profiles need a non-empty name); stored here so it survives re-registration. Author configuration, not runtime state.
Path to the source attribute to read (e.g., CurrentValue, or nested record.field). If not set, the adapter determines the default.
Identifier of the source entity (e.g. Loxone Control UUID, MQTT device ID)
Timestamp when execution started

Human-readable status or error message from the last deployment or configuration attempt. Reflects the current/live status — overwritten on every state change including successful transitions. For persistent error history, use LastDeploymentError / LastConfigurationError.
Successful executions folded into this bucket
The System ID (SID) is the unique technical name of an SAP system. It consists of three letters and uniquely identifies a system within a landscape.
The system number is a two-digit number assigned to an SAP system during installation. It is used to identify the SAP service (e.g. Dispatcher) on a specific port.
The tag value used for categorization and filtering.
Path to the target attribute to update on the mapped entity (e.g., Temperature, Humidity, or nested record.field)
Tax rate applied to energy transactions in the community
Temperature for AI response generation (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = creative).
The tertiary color of the theme
Sum of execution durations folded into this bucket (ms)
How this pipeline execution was initiated (Manual, Scheduled, Event, or Startup).
Theme color configuration for an application
The username is the name of the user that is used to authenticate with the external system.
String value of a ValueOverride entry. Encrypted at rest when the entry is flagged IsSecret.

Structured Helm value overrides. Deep-merged on top of ValuesYaml during deploy. Entries flagged IsSecret are stored encrypted. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed overrides (e.g. publicUri, clientId) are preserved across blueprint re-apply; a blueprint that needs to ship NEW default overrides only seeds them on fresh installs.

Full values.yaml content as a YAML string. Edited in a code editor or uploaded as a file in the Studio. Acts as the base layer of Helm values; ValueOverrides are deep-merged on top. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

records.description: Generic data point record for adapter data acquisition. Used in RecordArray attributes to store multiple named data points with their external identifiers and current values.

Names an AdapterPool in another tenant: the lending tenant and the pool's RtId inside it (AB#5271). Cross-tenant by nature, which is why it is a record of plain values rather than an association — a CK association cannot span tenant databases. Nothing enforces that the target exists; the controller resolves it per lease and refuses an unresolvable pool with a named reason.
Resolved mapping target for data acquisition. Built from DataPointMappings by the BuildMappingTargets node. Contains the source identifier, optional state name, and the external ID to poll/subscribe.

One UTC clock hour of pipeline-execution aggregates (AB#4370, AB#5583). Executions older than the retention window are folded into these buckets and then physically deleted; hours that still have retained executions are recomputed from them on every statistics sweep, so the buckets always cover every counted execution.

One audited Signal channel registration attempt (AB#5143). Appended server-side by the Communication Controller for every register/verify/delete attempt, including failures (captcha required, rate limited, wrong code). Stored newest-first on SignalChannel.RegistrationHistory, capped at the newest 50 entries; clients never write these.

A single Helm value override entry. Path is a dotted Helm values path (e.g. image.tag). Value is the override string. When IsSecret is true, Value is stored encrypted at rest and surfaced as a Kubernetes Secret reference at deploy time.

enums.description: Whether and to whom an adapter lends its process as a leasable pool member (AB#4924). NotShared (default) keeps the adapter private to its own tenant — the behaviour of every adapter in the estate today. Descendants lends to any descendant of the owning tenant, direct or indirect, resolved by the same breadth-first tenant walk as GET {tenantId}/v1/tenants/descendants (AB#5151). DescendantsAndSiblings additionally lends to tenants that share the owning tenant's parent. In every mode the optional LendingAllowedTenantIds allow-list narrows the resolved set further; it never widens it, so a tenant outside the subtree can not be granted a lease by listing it.
Indicates the current SignalR connection state of an adapter or pool operator.
Indicates whether a deployable entity has been successfully configured with its pipeline definitions and settings.

Tracks whether a deployable entity (adapter, application, pipeline, pool, or trigger) is currently deployed and active. Disabled means the entity cannot be deployed at all: Edge pools (no central operator CR), workloads missing Helm chart/version/repository, or pipelines/triggers whose adapter is Disabled. Deploy/Undeploy actions are rejected on Disabled entities.

Where a pool's adapter workloads are hosted. Cloud pools are auto-deployed by the central Communication Operator into the OctoMesh cluster; Edge pools must be installed and run by an external operator outside the central cluster.
Distribution channel of a Helm chart repository. Used as a label so the UI can colour-code dev vs release sources; the operator does not derive behavior from this value.

Which kind of chart a Helm repository serves. Adapters covers adapter and platform charts, Applications covers tenant-app charts. Used by the Communication Controller to pick a repository for a workload that carries no explicit HelmRepository association; never a label only.

Author-configured lifecycle policy of a deployable workload. AlwaysOn (default) keeps the workload running permanently. OnDemand lets the controller scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand (AB#4914); only valid for workloads whose deployed pipelines use exclusively wake-capable triggers. Auto is reserved for a future controller-decided mode and is rejected by validation until implemented. Leased (AB#4924) means the workload has no process of its own at all: its pipelines execute on an AdapterPool lent by an ancestor or sibling tenant, one lease per work item — see the LentFrom association to a LentAdapterPool mirror (AB#5271) and docs/concepts/shared-adapter-leasing.md. Leased is the BORROWER's mode and only ever that; an AdapterPool is its own workload type with a replica range and is not itself Leased.

Runtime lifecycle state of an OnDemand workload (AB#4914). Running: normal operation. Draining: idle timeout reached, scale-to-0 requested. Hibernated: scaled to 0 replicas on purpose — CommunicationState=Offline is expected and must not raise alarms. Waking: a demand signal triggered scale-to-1; consumers wait for ConfigurationState=Configured. AlwaysOn workloads stay Running permanently.

Scheduling class of a pipeline on a leased adapter pool (AB#4924), resolved from the pipeline's trigger node when the pipeline is SAVED and persisted here — not parsed from the YAML at dequeue time, so the scheduler reads a field and the Studio / octo-cli / MCP surfaces can show WHY a job sits where it does. Interactive is work a human is waiting for (HTTP request, manual run, Studio "execute now"). Batch is everything scheduled or event-driven. Within one tenant's turn in the round-robin rotation, Interactive is served before Batch; across tenants the class has no effect whatsoever. Mirrors OnDemandCapable: computed, persisted for display, and re-resolved whenever the pipeline is saved — so a pipeline edited to a different trigger changes class visibly, as a change, rather than as behaviour that quietly shifts.

Status of a pipeline execution lifecycle, from queued or running through completion or failure. Queued (AB#4924) precedes Running on a Leased workload: the execution entity exists from the moment the work item is enqueued, so one execution stays one entity from enqueue to completion and the Studio renders a continuous history instead of joining a queue and an execution source.
Indicates how a pipeline execution was initiated.

Which queue signal makes an adapter pool start another member (AB#4924). QueueDepth scales when the number of work items waiting for a lease crosses ScaleUpQueueDepthThreshold. QueueWaitSeconds scales when the oldest waiting item has waited longer than ScaleUpQueueWaitSeconds. QueueDepthOrWaitSeconds (default) scales on whichever fires first, which is the behaviour a pool wants in practice: depth catches a burst, wait time catches a slow trickle behind one long-running lease. CPU-based scaling is deliberately absent — a member waiting for a lease is idle by construction.

Audited action of a Signal channel registration attempt (AB#5143). Every register/verify/delete attempt against the tenant's SignalChannel — including failed ones — appends one entry with this action to the channel's RegistrationHistory. Adopted means the bridge already held a working account for the number, so register/verify were skipped and the definition went straight to Registered. ProfileUpdated records a display-name profile push (PUT /v1/profiles/{number}) — its detail carries the pushed name, the failure text for a rejected push on the displayName endpoint, or the cleared note (clearing never touches the bridge profile). Deleted is part of the audit vocabulary but a persisted Deleted entry never survives: a successful DELETE erases the definition including its history (fresh definition = fresh history); the system event trail still records the deletion.

Registration state of a tenant's Signal phone number against the Signal bridge (AB#5143). Unregistered means a definition exists but no registration was started (or a rate-limited attempt is pending retry). CodePending means the bridge accepted the register call and Signal sent an SMS verification code. Registered means the verify call succeeded and the number can send/receive. Failed means the last register attempt was rejected by the bridge (see LastError); a new register attempt is allowed.

description: Construction kit model for the OctoMesh Communication Controller. Defines adapters, adapter pools, deployment sites, pipelines, triggers, configurations, and execution tracking for data ingress and egress.
